paper.title: Language Generation with Infinite Contamination
paper.summary: Studies element and set generation when repetition-free presentations may contain finite, vanishing-rate, or constant-rate additive noise and may omit target elements. The theorem-card inventory covers the paper's principal results through Section 7 and Appendix B; Lean covers the main semantic priority and density constructions through Algorithm 9 and Theorem 7.8, while later lower bounds, the membership-query implementation, and appendix variants are explicitly registered as gaps.

formalization_scope.summary: The formalization has complete semantic interfaces and explicit-enumeration paths through Theorem 7.8, including Algorithms 6--9 and the element-density transfer. The complete selected-result inventory also records the later bounded-displacement lower bounds, finite-contamination corollary, membership-query implementation, and Appendix B variants with their actual partial or zero Lean coverage.
specializations: Theorems 5.1, 5.4, 6.1, 6.5, 6.11, 6.14, and 7.8 are packaged for a collection supplied by an explicit countable enumeration.
Theorems 6.15--6.18 make the paper's shared ambient canonical-order compatibility explicit.
The development is semantic and classical and does not establish computability or complexity bounds.
gaps: Theorem 6.14 is formalized for 0 < c < 1; the printed c = 1 sufficiency endpoint is not justified because its premise permits all observations to be noise.
The full source-level presentation packaging around Algorithm 2 remains separately tracked as partial, and the computable membership-query Corollary 4.5 has no machine-level formalization.

Corollary 6.20, Theorem 6.21, Theorems 7.6--7.7 and 7.9--7.11, and Appendix Theorems B.2--B.3 are not end-to-end Lean theorems; cards expose any reusable formalized components rather than overstating coverage.
The printed boundedness constant in Theorem 7.7 and the equality endpoint in Appendix Theorem B.3 are source-level gaps recorded in their cards.

audit_refs.scope: Direct AI-assisted comparison of the twenty-seven selected source-result groups against the SHA-256-pinned arXiv v1 PDF, including later bounded-displacement and Appendix B results and their recorded source gaps; no human certification is claimed.
The generated registry audit resolves every P17 claim-linked declaration; this checks Lean names and dependencies, not paper correspondence.

claim_inventory.scope_description: Twenty-seven source-centered groups covering the semantic definitions, principal numbered results through Section 7, the independent membership-query corollary, and the two Appendix B generation variants.
exclusions: Unnumbered proof-only observations and supporting results subsumed into a registered main-result group.

Appendix B supporting lemmas and Theorem B.4 are grouped into the Appendix B.3 threshold card rather than duplicated as independent headline cards.
claim_inventory.notes: Complete is relative to the selected source-result surface, not every proof lemma. Partial and source-qualified results retain explicit zero-coverage components so gaps are visible rather than inferred from missing declarations.

claims.statement_summary: A countable collection exists for which identification in the limit is impossible even when every presentation is M-bounded for any fixed M greater than one.

Since a displacement factor below one is impossible for an infinite canonical enumeration, the printed boundedness constant cannot be literal; the card records the supported 1 + 1/k reading.

claims.title: Finite k-language classes have a one-over-k noise threshold
claims.statement_summary: For k at least two, every k-language class is generatable below noise rate 1/k, while the paper claims a k-language counterexample at and above 1/k.

source_assessment.notes: The necessity proof's canonical stream has noise fraction 1/k + o(1), but the paper's c-noise definition requires an eventual pointwise bound by c. At c = 1/k, nonmultiples of k violate that bound, so the proof establishes rates strictly above 1/k but not the printed equality endpoint. The strict-below sufficiency is stated separately as Theorem B.4.

formalization.notes: Neither the strict-below construction nor a corrected strict-above impossibility theorem is formalized in P17.

relations.notes: Specializes the general constant-noise characterization to all finite classes of a fixed cardinality.
